title.en: The forgotten tiffin box: why does food spoil?

text.en: Disha finds her lunch box, forgotten since Friday, with an uttapam inside. When she opens it, a foul smell comes out and the uttapam has coloured patches. What happened?

Detective Disha wants to solve the mystery. Her elder brother Aditya tells her that the coloured patches are mould. Mould is made up of a colony of thousands of tiny living things called microbes.
Microbes are so tiny that we need a microscope to see them. They are found in soil, water, the air around us, in plants, animals and even inside us.
Some microbes help us, for example in making curd and in digesting food. Others change the taste and smell of food, as in the uttapam.
Why do some foods spoil faster? A slice of bread left outside got coloured patches in two days, but pickles made two months ago were still good, because they were covered with oil.
Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature to grow. If we remove any one of these we can stop them in their tracks.
Eating spoiled food by mistake can cause an upset stomach. Many people feel ill and need rest and a doctor's advice.
(additional, not in the textbook) Always smell, look and check the date on food before eating it, and throw away food that smells bad or has mould.

problem.en: Why did the uttapam in the tiffin box spoil?

text.en: It was left for three days in a closed box.
Microbes grew on it using the moisture and air.

why.en: They need moisture, air and warmth.

text.en: They changed its smell and made mould patches.

prompt.en: Explain why a slice of bread spoils but oily pickle does not.

requiredIdeas.en: Microbes need moisture and air to grow
Oil keeps out air in pickles
Bread has moisture and is open to air

points.en: Microbes are tiny living things found everywhere.
Mould is a colony of microbes.
Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature.
